question: Under the original Greek Recovery Plan, medical equipment was meant to be delivered to 80 hospitals by June 2026. On 18 June 2026, the project in question, which had an initial budget of around EUR 80 million, was excluded from the Recovery Fund and the corresponding target was removed from the revised plan.

On 31 August 2026, the Minister of Health stated that the project had not been cancelled but had been included in the sectoral development plan on 14 July and that it was due to be delivered within the year. This delay meant that the cost was transferred from the European programme to national resources. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
On what basis did it approve the removal of this target from the Greek Recovery Plan?
What amount of European funding was ultimately not used for the procurement of the medical equipment and where was it reallocated?
How will it check that the equipment will actually be delivered to all the hospitals it was originally intended for at no additional cost to Greek taxpayers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.10.2026) On 8 May 2026, Greece made a reasoned request to the Commission to make a proposal to amend the Council Implementing Decision of 13 July 2021 in accordance with Article 21(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/2411 on the grounds that the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) is partially no longer achievable because of objective circumstances2.

In this context, Greece explained that, due to unexpected delays related to public procurement procedures, measure 16795 ‘Health infrastructure’ was partially no longer achievable. Specifically, delays affected the subproject for the procurement and delivery of medical equipment to hospitals.

On this basis, the relevant milestone was removed from the Greek RRP as well as the associated estimated costing (which is indicative and ex-ante). The Greek authorities communicated that they would implement this subproject through national funding. In line with this, Greece requested to proportionally reduce the estimated costing of the measure from EUR 317 000 000 to EUR 254 483 835.

The resources freed up by this downscale were re-allocated to other measures in the Greek RRP which were upscaled, such as measure 16783 ‘Implementation of the National Public Health Prevention Program “Spiros Doxiadis”’.

As the subproject for the procurement and delivery of medical equipment to hospitals of measure 16795 ‘Health infrastructure’ is no longer included in the Greek RRP, it is not for the Commission to check its fulfilment.
